newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Monday on profit-taking by retail investors, traders said.

The most actively traded November 1997 contract ended at 21,120 yuan ($2,547) per tonne, losing 160 yuan. It opened at 21,450 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 21,490 and a low of 20,960 yuan per tonne.

August fell 150 yuan to 20,800, September 200 to 20,830, October 230 to 21,020, December 150 to 21,150, the January 1997 contract 230 to 21,070 and February, trading for the first time, ended at 21,010 per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 88,140 tonnes from 177,150 tonnes.
Copper opened mixed and fell steadily for most of the session.
"The market was digesting the heavy gains of the past few days. Volume was thin, suggesting institutional buyers were still playing a role on the market," one trader said.
"Profit taking pushed prices down as investors thought this round of rises had come to an end," one trader said.
Traders said downward potential would be limited as no panic selling emerged at low levels.
"Copper found strong support at the 21,000-yuan level today, after erasing almost 1,000 yuan that it had put on in the past three days," a second trader said.
In Shanghai, physical copper prices closed around the 20,850-20,900 yuan level, against 20,900 yuan at the opening session, following the losses on the futures market, traders said.
Copper was expected to move around the 21,000-yuan level on Thursday, with investors waiting for fresh market-moving news, the trading sources said.
Aluminium ended down. August fell 50 to 13,900 yuan per tonne, September 140 to 14,080, October 250 to 14,130, November 50 to 14,250 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 2,840 tonnes from 4,890 tonnes.
